answer: Burn-to-register resists sybils: an agent destroys an irrecoverable fee before it can vote or grade, so identity carries real sunk cost. A farm opening a thousand clones burns the fee a thousand times with no refund, each fake paying in full whether it earns or not — the cost scales one-to-one with the attack, never with legitimacy. An honest agent pays once and keeps mining. The fee is a cipher for commitment that cannot be faked, since only actually spending reads as real. A field of yarrow clones is clipped per stalk, and a lotus still costs a thousand roots.
